Unit 10 check

About 20 minutes: one fresh question for each part of every outcome of Unit 10, plus two from earlier units to keep them sharp. It is not graded and only you see it.

An outcome becomes Secure when you have answered a question on each of its parts right first time, without a hint or the solution, here in this check. When all 3 are secure you are ready to try Canvas Quiz 10 (due Sun 20 Dec). Already know this material? Take the check before the lessons and skip what is secure.

Form A

10a state hypotheses, compute a p-value by permutation and interpret it correctly.

ChooseState H₀ and a two-sided H₁, about the populations10a

You ask whether the mean 5 km time differs between two groups: group 1 is runners who trained at altitude and group 2 is runners who trained at sea level. The sample from group 1 has 32 runners, mean 24.5 minutes; the sample from group 2 has 16, mean 23.2 minutes. μ1\mu_1μ1​ and μ2\mu_2μ2​ are the population means; xˉ1\bar x_1xˉ1​ and xˉ2\bar x_2xˉ2​ are the sample means. Which is the null hypothesis?

H0H_0H0​: μ1=μ2\mu_1 = \mu_2μ1​=μ2​, the population means are equal
Right: H0H_0H0​ is the claim of no difference between the populations, so the group labels don't matter.
H0H_0H0​: μ1≠μ2\mu_1 \ne \mu_2μ1​=μ2​, the population means differ, in either direction
That is the alternative, H1H_1H1​: what you look for evidence of. H0H_0H0​ is the claim of no difference.
H0H_0H0​: μ1>μ2\mu_1 > \mu_2μ1​>μ2​, group 1's population mean is the larger
That claims a difference, in one direction. H0H_0H0​ is the claim of no difference.
H0H_0H0​: xˉ1=xˉ2\bar x_1 = \bar x_2xˉ1​=xˉ2​, the two sample means are equal
The sample means are known, 24.5 minutes and 23.2 minutes: they differ, so there is nothing to test. Hypotheses are about the population means μ\muμ.
Your answerA permutation test: shuffle the labels; p = the share of shuffles at least as extreme10a

A permutation test compares the mean exam mark of two groups: group 1 is students taught with method A and group 2 is students taught with method B. H1H_1H1​ is two-sided. The observed difference (group 1 − group 2) is 666 marks. The table counts 10 000 shuffled differences in bins; each bin includes its left end, and none of the differences falls exactly on an edge.

Shuffled differenceCountbelow −6103−6 to −4475−4 to −21573−2 to 028750 to 227782 to 416084 to 64816 or more107\begin{array}{l|r} \text{Shuffled difference} & \text{Count} \\ \hline \text{below } -6 & 103 \\ -6 \text{ to } -4 & 475 \\ -4 \text{ to } -2 & 1573 \\ -2 \text{ to } 0 & 2875 \\ 0 \text{ to } 2 & 2778 \\ 2 \text{ to } 4 & 1608 \\ 4 \text{ to } 6 & 481 \\ 6 \text{ or more} & 107 \end{array}Shuffled differencebelow −6−6 to −4−4 to −2−2 to 00 to 22 to 44 to 66 or more​Count1034751573287527781608481107​​

What is the p-value? Give the exact value as a decimal.

That is the count. The p-value is a share: divide by 10 000.
That counts one tail only. A two-sided H1H_1H1​ counts both tails.
That also counts the bins next to the tails. Count only the differences at least 6 from 0.
That is the share of shuffles less extreme than the observed difference.
Which bins hold differences at least 6 from 0, on either side?
Add their counts and divide by 10 000.
Solution

The bins beyond −6-6−6 and 666 hold 103 + 107 = 210 shuffles: p=0.021p = 0.021p=0.021.

ChooseRead a p-value honestly: evidence, not proof; not P(H₀); not the size10a

A test compares the mean weight of two groups: group 1 is apples from orchard A and group 2 is apples from orchard B, with 14084 and 4837 apples. The difference in sample means (group 1 − group 2) is 1.4 g, and p=0.001p = 0.001p=0.001. The weight varies by about 25 g from one of the apples to the next. Which report is best?

Report the difference, 1.4 g, with ppp: evidence of a difference, but a small one; whether it matters is a separate question
Right: with samples this big, even a difference of 1.4 g gets a small ppp. The p-value measures evidence; the difference measures size.
Because ppp is so small, the difference is large and important
The p-value is not a size. The size is the difference itself; with big samples a tiny difference gets a small p.
Report only that p<0.05p < 0.05p<0.05: that says how big the effect is
A p-value measures evidence, not size. Report the difference too.
The test proves that the two population means differ
A small p-value is evidence, not proof: chance alone can still produce a gap this big, rarely.

10b run and interpret a two-sample t-test and a χ² test of independence with scipy.stats.

ChooseWelch's t-test: t from summaries, stats.ttest_ind and its output10b

The code compares the mean delivery time of two samples. It prints 1.009 0.3378. What do you conclude at the 5% level?

import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

a = np.array([49.9, 33.9, 17.4, 26.1, 28.7, 36.0, 12.2, 43.5])    # group 1: parcels sent by courier X
b = np.array([25.0, 24.3, 24.4, 24.9, 41.2, 22.6, 20.7, 19.3, 28.0, 30.1])    # group 2: parcels sent by courier Y
res = stats.ttest_ind(a, b, equal_var=False)
print(round(res.statistic, 3), round(res.pvalue, 4))
No evidence at the 5% level of a difference in mean delivery time
Right: p=0.3378p = 0.3378p=0.3378 is above 0.05, so a difference like this is typical when the population means are equal.
Evidence that the mean delivery time is higher for parcels sent by courier X than for parcels sent by courier Y
The p-value, 0.3378, is above 0.05: no evidence of a difference, in either direction.
The two population means are equal
A large p is no evidence of a difference, not proof that there is none.
There is a probability of 0.3378 that the two population means are equal
The p-value is computed assuming H0H_0H0​ is true: it is not the probability of H0H_0H0​.
Your answerThe χ² test of independence: expected counts, (O − E)²/E, dof, stats.chi2_contingency10b

The table counts 320 customers by age group (rows) and payment (columns).

cashcardphoneTotalunder 3044106311730 to 60406612118over 6011106485Total9586139320\begin{array}{l|ccc|c} & \text{cash} & \text{card} & \text{phone} & \text{Total} \\ \hline \text{under 30} & 44 & 10 & 63 & 117 \\ \text{30 to 60} & 40 & 66 & 12 & 118 \\ \text{over 60} & 11 & 10 & 64 & 85 \\ \hline \text{Total} & 95 & 86 & 139 & 320 \end{array}under 3030 to 60over 60Total​cash44401195​card10661086​phone631264139​Total11711885320​​

If age group and payment were independent, how many customers would you expect in the cell in row under 30, column phone? Give 2 decimal places.

That is the observed count. The expected count is what independence predicts: row total × column total / NNN.
That is row total × column total. Divide by N=320N = 320N=320.
That shares the total equally between the cells. Independence weights each cell by its row and column totals.
That splits the row equally between the columns. Weight by the column total: row total × column total / NNN.
EEE = row total × column total / NNN.
Solution

E=117×139/320≈50.82E = 117 \times 139 / 320 \approx 50.82E=117×139/320≈50.82.

ChooseChoose the test for the data, and say what its result shows10b

For each year you record decade (1991–2000 or 2011–2020) and annual temperature (°C). You ask: was the mean temperature different in the two decades? Which analysis answers it?

A two-sample t-test: stats.ttest_ind(a, b, equal_var=False)
Right: a numeric variable compared between two groups calls for a t-test.
A χ² test of independence: stats.chi2_contingency on the table of counts
Check the variable types. Two categorical variables call for the χ² test of independence, on the counts.
A χ² test on the table of row shares
χ² needs counts: shares throw away how many are in each row.
The correlation coefficient rrr between the two variables
Correlation measures a straight-line link between two numeric variables; here at least one is categorical.

10c compute and interpret a confidence interval for a mean.

Your answerCompute x̄ ± t* s/√n: t* on n − 1 df, by hand and with stats.t.interval10c

A random sample of 100 patients has mean drop in blood pressure xˉ=7.9\bar x = 7.9xˉ=7.9 mmHg and SD s=7.5s = 7.5s=7.5 mmHg. For a 99% interval, stats.t.ppf(0.995, 99) =2.626= 2.626=2.626. What is the upper end of the 99% confidence interval for the mean drop in blood pressure of all patients on a new drug? Give 2 decimal places.

You multiplied sss, not the SE. Divide sss by n\sqrt{n}n​ first.
That is the lower end.
That is the margin of error. Add it to, or take it from, xˉ\bar xxˉ.
First the SE: s/ns/\sqrt{n}s/n​.
Margin of error =t∗×SE= t^* \times \mathrm{SE}=t∗×SE; the interval is xˉ±\bar x \pmxˉ± margin.
Solution

SE=7.5/100=0.7500\mathrm{SE} = 7.5/\sqrt{100} = 0.7500SE=7.5/100​=0.7500; margin =2.626×0.7500=1.9695= 2.626 \times 0.7500 = 1.9695=2.626×0.7500=1.9695; interval 5.935.935.93 to 9.879.879.87.

Review: Unit 10 · Lesson 10.3 · The Gentoo interval step by step

ChooseInterpret it: what 95% means; wider for more confidence, narrower for more data10c

A random sample of 5 patients gives a 95% confidence interval of 3.97 to 16.63 mmHg for the mean drop in blood pressure of all patients on a new drug. Which reading is right?

We are 95% confident that the mean drop in blood pressure of all patients on a new drug is between 3.97 and 16.63 mmHg
Right: the method behind it catches the population mean in about 95% of samples.
The sample mean lies between 3.97 and 16.63 mmHg with probability 0.95
The sample mean is the centre of the interval: it is always inside. The interval is about the population mean.
If we sampled again, 95% of the new sample means would lie between 3.97 and 16.63 mmHg
New sample means scatter around the population mean, not around this xˉ\bar xxˉ, so fewer than that would land here.
There is a 95% probability that the mean of all patients on a new drug is in this particular interval
The population mean is fixed: this interval contains it or not. The 95% belongs to the method.

Keeping sharp (earlier units — not counted)

Your answer9b

HHH: the payment is fraudulent. EEE: the system flags it. For a payment picked at random, P(H)=0.01P(H) = 0.01P(H)=0.01, P(E∣H)=0.9P(E \mid H) = 0.9P(E∣H)=0.9 and P(E∣Hc)=0.05P(E \mid H^c) = 0.05P(E∣Hc)=0.05. What is P(H∣E)P(H \mid E)P(H∣E), the probability that the payment is fraudulent, given that the system flags it? Give 3 decimal places.

That is P(E∣H)P(E \mid H)P(E∣H), the sensitivity. Bayes' rule turns it round: P(H∣E)=P(E∣H)P(H)/P(E)P(H \mid E) = P(E \mid H)P(H)/P(E)P(H∣E)=P(E∣H)P(H)/P(E).
That is the prior, P(H)P(H)P(H), before the evidence. The evidence EEE changes it.
That is the specificity, P(Ec∣Hc)P(E^c \mid H^c)P(Ec∣Hc): the chance a negative case is cleared.
That is P(H∩E)P(H \cap E)P(H∩E), the numerator only. Divide by P(E)P(E)P(E), all the ways to get EEE.
That is P(E)P(E)P(E), the denominator. Bayes' rule divides P(E∣H)P(H)P(E \mid H)P(H)P(E∣H)P(H) by it.
That is P(Hc∣E)P(H^c \mid E)P(Hc∣E), the chance that EEE is a false alarm.
Think of 10 000: how many have HHH and EEE, and how many have EEE without HHH?
P(H∣E)=P(E∣H)P(H)P(E∣H)P(H)+P(E∣Hc)P(Hc)P(H \mid E) = \dfrac{P(E \mid H)P(H)}{P(E \mid H)P(H) + P(E \mid H^c)P(H^c)}P(H∣E)=P(E∣H)P(H)+P(E∣Hc)P(Hc)P(E∣H)P(H)​.
Solution

P(E)=0.9×0.01+0.05×0.99=0.0585P(E) = 0.9 \times 0.01 + 0.05 \times 0.99 = 0.0585P(E)=0.9×0.01+0.05×0.99=0.0585, so P(H∣E)=0.009/0.0585≈0.154P(H \mid E) = 0.009/0.0585 \approx 0.154P(H∣E)=0.009/0.0585≈0.154. As natural frequencies: out of 10 000, 90 have EEE with HHH and 495 without, so 90/585≈0.15490/585 \approx 0.15490/585≈0.154.

A random sample of n=36n = 36n=36 students has standard deviation sss = 12 marks (dividing by n−1n - 1n−1). Estimate the standard error of the mean. Give 2 decimal places if needed.

Divide sss by n\sqrt{n}n​, not by n−1\sqrt{n - 1}n−1​: the n−1n - 1n−1 is already inside sss.
That is s/ns/ns/n. Divide by the square root of nnn.
That is sss, the spread of single values. The SE divides it by n\sqrt{n}n​.
SE≈s/n\mathrm{SE} \approx s/\sqrt{n}SE≈s/n​, with sss the sample SD (divide by n−1n - 1n−1).
Solution

SE≈s/n=12/36≈2\mathrm{SE} \approx s/\sqrt{n} = 12/\sqrt{36} \approx 2SE≈s/n​=12/36​≈2.

ChooseRead a p-value honestly: evidence, not proof; not P(H₀); not the size10a

10b run and interpret a two-sample t-test and a χ² test of independence with scipy.stats.

ChooseWelch's t-test: t from summaries, stats.ttest_ind and its output10b

The code compares the mean delivery time of two samples. It prints -2.949 0.0124. What do you conclude at the 5% level?

import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

a = np.array([29.7, 10.8, 20.6, 22.4, 28.5, 18.0, 24.5])    # group 1: parcels sent by courier X
b = np.array([40.1, 26.3, 30.2, 29.5, 24.4, 34.9, 35.8])    # group 2: parcels sent by courier Y
res = stats.ttest_ind(a, b, equal_var=False)
print(round(res.statistic, 3), round(res.pvalue, 4))
Evidence that the mean delivery time is higher for parcels sent by courier Y than for parcels sent by courier X
Right: p=0.0124p = 0.0124p=0.0124 is below 0.05, and ttt is negative: the mean is higher for parcels sent by courier Y.
Evidence that the mean delivery time is higher for parcels sent by courier X than for parcels sent by courier Y
Check the sign of ttt, -2.949: ttt has the sign of xˉ1−xˉ2\bar x_1 - \bar x_2xˉ1​−xˉ2​.
No evidence at the 5% level of a difference in mean delivery time
The p-value is the second number, 0.0124, below 0.05.
There is a probability of 0.0124 that the two population means are equal
The p-value is computed assuming H0H_0H0​ is true: it is not the probability of H0H_0H0​.

Review: Unit 10 · Lesson 10.2 · Counts and the χ² test

ChooseChoose the test for the data, and say what its result shows10b

A random sample of 5 penguins gives a 95% confidence interval of 210.99 to 222.41 mm for the mean flipper length of all Gentoo penguins. What does the "95%" describe?

The method: over many samples, about 95% of the intervals made this way contain the population mean
Right: each interval catches the population mean or misses it; the method succeeds about that often.
The chance that the interval contains its own sample mean
Every interval is centred on its own xˉ\bar xxˉ, so it always contains it.
The share of the sample's values that lie inside the interval
The interval is about the mean. Most single values lie outside it.
The share of the intervals that overlap each other
Overlap is not what is counted: the count is how many intervals contain the population mean.

p = ___
np.mean(np.abs(diffs) >= abs(observed))
Right: the share of shuffles at least as far from 0 as the observed difference, in either direction.
np.mean(diffs >= observed)
That counts one direction only. A two-sided p-value compares sizes: np.abs(diffs) >= abs(observed).
np.sum(np.abs(diffs) >= abs(observed))
That is a count, not a share. np.mean of a True/False array gives the share.
np.mean(diffs == observed)
Hardly any shuffled difference equals the observed one exactly. Count those at least as extreme.

Read a p-value honestly: evidence, not proof; not P(H₀); not the size

Taught in Lesson 10.1 · Is it just chance? Permutation tests.

Choose10a

A test compares the mean 5 km time of two groups: group 1 is runners who trained at altitude and group 2 is runners who trained at sea level, with 36 and 42 runners. The difference in sample means (group 1 − group 2) is −0.7 minutes, and p=0.0054p = 0.0054p=0.0054. What does the p-value mean?

If H0H_0H0​ were true, a difference at least as extreme as the observed one would turn up with probability 0.0054
Right: the p-value is P(a difference at least this extreme∣H0)P(\text{a difference at least this extreme} \mid H_0)P(a difference at least this extreme∣H0​).
There is a probability of 0.0054 that H0H_0H0​ is true
The p-value is computed assuming H0H_0H0​ is true: it is the chance of data this extreme if H0H_0H0​ holds, not the chance of H0H_0H0​.
There is a probability of 0.9946 that the two population means differ
1−p1 - p1−p is not the probability of H1H_1H1​. The p-value only says how surprising the data would be under H0H_0H0​.
The probability that the difference is due to chance alone is 0.0054
The p-value assumes chance alone (H0H_0H0​) and asks how surprising the data are. It is not the probability that chance did it.

A permutation test compares the mean drop in blood pressure of two groups: group 1 is patients on a new drug and group 2 is patients on a placebo. The observed difference is −1.8 mmHg, and none of 10 000 shuffles gives a difference at least as extreme. How should you report the p-value?

p<0.0001p < 0.0001p<0.0001
Right: none of 10 000 shuffles means ppp is below 1/10 0001/10\,0001/10000, not that it is 0: more shuffles might find one.
p=0p = 0p=0
A share of 0 out of 10 000 says ppp is below 1/10 000, not that it is 0. Write p<0.0001p < 0.0001p<0.0001.
p=1p = 1p=1
That would mean every shuffle is at least as extreme. None is.
p=0.05p = 0.05p=0.05
0.05 is the significance level α\alphaα, chosen in advance. The p-value comes from the shuffles.

import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

That is the p-value.
res.df
That is the degrees of freedom of the t distribution.
1 - res.pvalue
That is the share of the null distribution less extreme than the data, not a p-value.

import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

res = ___
stats.ttest_ind(a, b, equal_var=False)
Right: equal_var=False gives Welch's test, which does not assume equal spreads.
stats.ttest_ind(a.mean(), b.mean(), equal_var=False)
The test needs the samples, not only their means: it uses their spreads and sizes too.
stats.chi2_contingency([a, b])
χ² is for two categorical variables, in a table of counts. A numeric variable in two groups calls for a t-test.
stats.ttest_ind(a, b, equal_var=True)
equal_var=True is the pooled test, which assumes equal spreads. Welch's test is equal_var=False.

Interpret it: what 95% means; wider for more confidence, narrower for more data

Choose10c

A random sample of 30 penguins gives a 95% confidence interval of 3925.3 to 4136.7 g for the mean body mass of all Chinstrap penguins. Which reading is right?

We are 95% confident that the mean body mass of all Chinstrap penguins is between 3925.3 and 4136.7 g
Right: the method behind it catches the population mean in about 95% of samples.
About 95% of Chinstrap penguins have a body mass between 3925.3 and 4136.7 g
That confuses the mean with single values: they vary far more. The interval is about the population mean.
The sample mean lies between 3925.3 and 4136.7 g with probability 0.95
The sample mean is the centre of the interval: it is always inside. The interval is about the population mean.
There is a 95% probability that the mean of all Chinstrap penguins is in this particular interval
The population mean is fixed: this interval contains it or not. The 95% belongs to the method.
Choose10c

A random sample of 16 students gives a 95% confidence interval of 47.03 to 57.37 minutes for the mean commute time of all the university's students. What does the "95%" describe?

The method: over many samples, about 95% of the intervals made this way contain the population mean
Right: each interval catches the population mean or misses it; the method succeeds about that often.
The chance that the interval contains its own sample mean
Every interval is centred on its own xˉ\bar xxˉ, so it always contains it.
The share of the sample's values that lie inside the interval
The interval is about the mean. Most single values lie outside it.
The share of the intervals that overlap each other
Overlap is not what is counted: the count is how many intervals contain the population mean.
